- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing the true mean-reversion path.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+ → 85+) are common, followed by exaggerated corrections.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after peaks.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, suggesting a systematic overconfidence in upward momentum.
- Mean reversion is not adequately captured; model fails to adjust downward when recent history shows declining trends.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10–15 days, then overly pessimistic in the last 10–15 days.
